title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcement and improve circuit-breaker regional failover
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: After a 2026-02-24 incident where several regional pools triggered aggressive load-shedding during a transient backend spike, we observed end-user error rates exceed the SLO window and automatic regional failover kicking in prematurely. Root cause: the SLO enforcer used a short evaluation window combined with an optimistic circuit-breaker backoff, causing oscillation between regions and unnecessary shedding of healthy traffic.

Motivation: Restore stable graceful degradation behavior under transient backend errors, prevent premature regional failovers, and ensure the SLO evaluation is robust to short spikes. This hotfix tightens enforcement logic, adds extra state reconciliation during failover, and patches an off-by-one in the sliding-window aggregator.

Changes included: - Increase SLO evaluation window from 30s to 90s for request-error-rate SLOs to reduce sensitivity to short spikes. - Add hysteresis to circuit-breaker transitions (cooldown and minimum-open intervals). - Improve regional_proxy reconciliation: check remote region health via aggregated metrics and avoid immediate traffic reroute unless sustained degradation detected. - Fix off-by-one bug in sliding-window implementation that undercounted successful responses when windows wrapped. - Add observability: new metrics (slo_enforcer.window_size, circuit_breaker.hysteresis_count, regional_proxy.reconciliation_attempts) and a dashboard link. - Test coverage: add unit and integration tests for new windowing, hysteresis, and reconciliation flows.

Testing & CI: Unit tests and integration tests added. Ran canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic spike tests; observed no premature failover and stable error budget burn. CI: lint, unit, integration, e2e and security scans passed (see ci_checks).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge hotfix to main and deploy to canary (us-west-2) with 1% of traffic. 2) Monitor slo_enforcer and circuit_breaker metrics for 30 minutes. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% across regions if no regressions. 4) If new regressions observed, automatic rollback using existing rollout policy.

Related: ENG-1892 tracks long-term SLO tuning work; SRE-403 documents the incident and postmortem.

Notes: This is a targeted hotfix focused on stability; long-term changes (adaptive windows, ML-based anomaly detection) will be tracked in ENG-2017.
commits: Fix: expand SLO window and add hysteresis to circuit-breaker
Fix: regional_proxy reconciliation logic to consult aggregated health before failover
Test: add unit and integration tests for windowing and hysteresis
Docs: incident notes and dashboard pointer
review_comments: Liam Patel: Please add a short note about the potential latency impact of increasing the evaluation window. Is 90s reasonable for low-latency SLOs?

Ava Chen: Responded: We measured median latency impact at +2ms in canary; added note in rollout and a dashboard alert to watch for latency increases. 90s chosen as conservative tradeoff to avoid oscillation; long-term work will explore adaptive windows.
Sofia Ramirez: Approved after adding unit test for window wrap-around and confirming metric names. Left a nit for log formatting.
Noah Zhang: Verified reconciliation logic with simulated cross-region metrics; requested adding a reconciliation_attempts metric which was added in this PR.
release_notes: Hotfix: SLO enforcement and circuit-breaker behavior tightened to prevent premature regional failover and excessive load-shedding during short backend spikes. Adds observability metrics and tests.
notes_for_oncall: If rollback required: revert to previous enforcer config (main~1) and redeploy; watch slo_enforcer.window_size, circuit_breaker.state_transitions and regional_proxy.reconciliation_attempts. Escalate to SRE if error budget burn exceeds thresholds after rollback.
